info.title: Knocklog API
info.summary: Analytics for AI agents: which AI agents visit a website, whether they are real, and what AI assistants send it.
info.description:
Knocklog shows which AI agents and crawlers visit a website, whether each one is who it claims to be, what they read, and the visitors and leads AI assistants send.

**Start without an account:** `GET /v1/scan` checks how a site treats AI agents, `POST /v1/classify` identifies one request and `GET /v1/agents` lists known agents.

**Measure a site:** `POST /v1/projects` creates a project and returns two keys and install code. Send traffic with the ingest key (`POST /v1/events` from a collector, or `POST /v1/logs` with access logs) and read the report with the admin key (`GET /v1/traffic`).

**Keys.** Send them as `Authorization: Bearer <key>`. The ingest key (`kl_ing_…`) can only send traffic; it is safe in a collector on the site. The admin key (`kl_adm_…`) reads reports and manages the project; keep it private. Both are shown once, when the project is created.

**For AI agents:** the same features are available over MCP at `https://api.knocklog.ai/mcp` (keys as arguments), `https://api.knocklog.ai/mcp/directory` (public tools, no sign-in) and `https://api.knocklog.ai/mcp/account` (OAuth sign-in).

Errors are JSON: `{"error": {"code": "…", "message": "…"}}`. Fields may be added to responses at any time; clients should ignore fields they do not know.

get.description: The directory of AI agents and crawlers: operator, purpose, User-Agent and robots.txt tokens, whether they obey robots.txt, what the operator publishes to recognise them, and the operator's documentation.

post.description: Says whether a request came from an AI agent, which one, and whether it really is that agent. Pass at least the User-Agent or the headers; the IP address and URL make the answer more precise.

get.summary: Check how a site treats AI agents
get.description: Reads the site's robots.txt, homepage, llms.txt and markdown support, and returns a score from 0 to 100, what each known agent may access, and what to fix. Results are cached for a short time.

post.description: Creates a project for a website. Returns the ingest and admin keys (shown only once) and install instructions with ready-to-paste code for the site's hosting. With `email`, the weekly summary is offered to that address, which must confirm by email.

email.description: Optional: send the weekly summary to this address after it is confirmed

post.description:
Sends up to 100 requests the site received. With the ingest key they are classified and stored in the project. Without a key they are only classified and returned, so anyone can try the classifier on their own traffic.

Send each agent request with its IP address and headers (never cookies or authorization). For people's page views, send only HTML pages and keep the query string to utm_* parameters.

202.description: Accepted. With a key: counts of what was stored. Without a key: one detection per event.

post.description: Imports Apache or Nginx access log lines (combined format, as in cPanel Raw Access). Send the lines as text/plain, or as JSON `{"log": "…", "host": "…"}`. Up to 2 MiB per request; send larger logs in consecutive chunks. Re-sending a chunk is safe: duplicates are ignored.

parameters.name: host
parameters.description: Subdomain the log belongs to, if not the project's main host

parameters.name: ips
parameters.description: Whether the first field is the visitor's IP (direct) or a proxy's (proxy)

parameters.name: live
parameters.description: Set by log shippers that send every few minutes, so the project is watched like a live collector

get.description: The project's plan, this month's usage and the next plan up. Works with either key.

What agents did on the site over the last N days: agent requests and people's page views, agents by class and by name, how many were verified or impostors, the pages agents read most, visits and leads sent by AI assistants, and a daily series. Companies that visited are listed on Business and up. The window is capped by the plan's history.

403.description: The key cannot do this (for example an ingest key on an admin endpoint)

get.description: Plan and usage, every benefit with whether the plan includes it and whether it is available today, when data last arrived, the summary contact, a checklist of first steps with live status, and the code snippets for the site (leads from AI, badge).

post.description: Sets where Knocklog sends events as they happen (see Webhooks). `webhookUrl` takes a Slack incoming webhook or any public https endpoint (Business and up); `null` removes it. When a URL is set, the response includes a `webhookSecret` once: JSON deliveries carry `x-knocklog-signature: sha256=<HMAC-SHA256 of the body>`. `companyEmails` turns the email to the contact when a company visits on or off (Enterprise). `test: true` sends a test event.

post.description: For sites whose DNS is on Cloudflare. Send a Cloudflare API token with Workers Scripts (edit), Workers Routes (edit) and Zone (read) permissions; `GET /v1/account` returns a link that creates one with exactly these permissions. Knocklog deploys the collector Worker and its routes and does not keep the token.

post.summary: A visitor sent by an AI assistant became a lead
post.description: A form sent or a WhatsApp, phone or email tap by someone who arrived from an AI assistant (needs leads.js on the site).

adminKey.description: Admin key (kl_adm_…): reads reports and manages the project. Keep it private.

AgentClass.description: training_crawler: collects content to train models. ai_search_crawler: indexes pages for AI search. user_action_agent: an assistant fetching a page because a person asked. agentic_browser: a browser driven by an AI. coding_agent: an AI coding tool fetching docs. search_engine: classic search. preview_fetcher: link previews. ads_checker: ad landing-page checks. automation_client: scripts and HTTP libraries. scraper: undeclared bots.

verification.description: What the operator publishes to recognise its agent

checkedAt.description: When the entry was last checked against docsUrl

isAgent.description: Any automated client: a known agent, a signed agent or a bot recognised by its behaviour

status.description: verified: the claim was confirmed. failed: there is positive evidence the claim is false. unverifiable: the operator publishes nothing that can be checked. not_checked: no identity was claimed.

steps.description: The checks that ran. Their names may change.

spoofed.description: The request claims a known agent's identity and the claim failed

reachable.description: false when the site answered nothing usable

homepage.description: Status, title, visible text and whether the page needs JavaScript to show its content

agents.description: What each known agent may access under robots.txt

timestamp.description: When the request reached the site

ip.description: Client IP address. Needed to verify agents. Not stored.

headers.description: Lower-case request headers: user-agent, accept, accept-language, referer, from, signature, signature-input, signature-agent. Never send cookies or authorization.

sampleRate.description: If people's page views are sampled, the share sent; each event then counts as 1/sampleRate

overlapping.description: Skipped because a live collector already covers that time

InstallPlan.description: Install options for the site's hosting, the recommended one first, each with steps and ready-to-paste code

agentShare.description: Page views by identified, genuine agents ÷ (those + people's page views)

previous.description: The same totals for the previous window, when the plan's history reaches it

aiLeads.description: Leads by assistant, action and page (Pro and up)

companies.description: Organizations whose own network people browsed from (Business and up)

agentCompanies.description: Companies behind agents and scripts (Business and up)

kind.description: business, education or government; other values may be added

interest.description: The visit included pricing, contact or similar pages

activity.description: When data first and last arrived, and the last 24 hours

actions.description: Code snippets for the site (leads from AI, badge) and how to complete each step
